synopsis: Dubai's iconic Burj Khalifa is enveloped in a living, self-mending engineered material that glows softly, extending across the city's architecture.

shots.prompt:
Shot 1, exactly 4 seconds at 24 fps, AERIAL. The camera flies high in the open sky, far ABOVE every rooftop, tower and mast in the city, and looks DOWN on it from there. The whole city lies below the camera and spreads across the frame from edge to edge; the horizon and open sky sit in the top third. Think satellite, helicopter or drone at altitude. The very first frame already contains BOTH the real city's recognisable landmark or skyline AND the advanced technology this episode is about, built at city scale and visibly running, so a viewer who sees only this one frame already knows which city it is and what it became. Something inside the city MOVES independently of the camera for the whole four seconds: transit pods travelling their line, craft crossing their corridor, cargo drones streaming between towers, light pulsing along a structure. One slow, single-direction camera move only, a straight descent or a forward glide, and the camera stays outdoors and above the structures for the entire four seconds. The shot holds one continuous unbroken view from first frame to last.

AERIAL. The camera descends slowly over Dubai. The Burj Khalifa, now draped in living engineered material, glows softly along its edges, visibly growing and shifting in subtle patterns. The city's skyline below is similarly adorned with this softly luminous, self-mending skin, stretching across buildings from edge to edge. Subtle energy pulses or organic movements are visible across the material. The camera performs a straight, slow descent.

Shot 2, exactly 4 seconds at 24 fps, GROUND LEVEL. After a hard cut, the camera stands at human eye height in a busy public place in the SAME city, at a completely different vantage point from shot 1. People go about ordinary daily life around the technology, walking, riding, trading, carrying and queueing, while autonomous machines work alongside them at the same easy pace. Every human figure reads at roughly one sixth of the frame height or smaller and stands in the middle ground or further back, seen from behind or in three-quarter view, so the crowd reads as movement and warmth at a distance. The nearest third of the frame is held by architecture, machinery, planting or open floor. Warm practical light from windows, canopies, lamps and the technology's own glow falls across the scene. Surfaces carry painted symbols and plain colour fields, so every surface stays clear of lettering. The same recognisable landmark stays readable in the background or on the horizon so the shots read as one city. One slow, single-direction camera move only, at a constant height.

GROUND LEVEL. The camera moves slowly at human eye height through a modern public concourse in Dubai, with surfaces made of the glowing, living engineered material. People walk casually, their forms small and distant, passing by planters of bio-luminescent flora. Autonomous maintenance bots glide across the floor, ensuring the material remains pristine. The Burj Khalifa's distinct silhouette is visible in the background, softly radiant. The camera moves slowly forward at a constant height.

Shot 3, exactly 4 seconds at 24 fps, MACHINE SCALE. After a hard cut, the camera is close to the advanced technology itself while it works: an autonomous builder arm laying material, a transit pod sliding through its guide, an energy column drawing light up its length, a fabricator filling a crate, a machine-tended canopy of growing green. The mechanism fills most of the frame and its motion is continuous, purposeful, precise and unhurried. Machined metal, glass and structural light carry fine surface detail. The recognisable landmark or skyline stays visible past the mechanism so the city remains identified. Human presence reads only as small distant figures far behind the machine. One slow, single-direction camera move only.

MACHINE SCALE. The camera is close to a section of the living engineered material covering a building facade. The intricate, organic texture of the material fills the frame, subtly shifting in color and light as it self-repairs and grows. Fine tendrils of light spread across its surface. Distant, small figures can be seen moving on a lower level, providing scale. The Burj Khalifa's upper spire is visible in the background, glowing softly. The camera slowly tracks horizontally along the facade.

Shot 4, exactly 4 seconds at 24 fps, WARM DETAIL. After a hard cut, the camera rests close on one small piece of everyday home life inside this advanced city: a lit balcony thick with plants above a glowing street, a small delivery drone settling onto a window ledge, laundry moving in warm air beside a luminous wall panel, a cat asleep on a warm machined sill, steam rising from a food counter, a child's bicycle leaning against a rail of light. The detail fills the frame and is lit warmly from inside the home. Motion is gentle and continuous: leaves stirring, steam curling, light breathing, the drone settling. Any person present reads as a small silhouette or a shoulder passing at the frame edge, well behind the subject. A sliver of the recognisable skyline or landmark sits softly out of focus in the background so the place stays identified. One slow, single-direction camera move only.

WARM DETAIL. The camera rests on a close-up of a small, integrated glowing planter on a window ledge inside a Dubai residence. The living material of the sill itself softly pulses with light, nurturing a small, vibrant plant. A sliver of the distant, softly glowing Burj Khalifa skyline is visible out of focus through the window. Gentle tendrils of light from the material slowly expand and contract. The camera slowly glides past the planter.

music: A single sustained sub-bass drone at one steady level for the whole duration, built from deep low-frequency air and distant structural resonance. It holds the same volume from the first second to the last, stays free of percussion, rhythm, melody, vocals and high frequencies, and ends mid-tone so the loop is seamless.
caption:
Dubai in 2512 has sheathed its iconic Burj Khalifa in living engineered material that grows, mends itself, and glows softly along every edge of the city. This innovation keeps the city's surfaces perpetually pristine, vibrant, and energy-efficient, while creating a unique organic aesthetic. Buildings shimmer with soft, bioluminescent light at night, pathways are lined with self-repairing surfaces, and the air carries a faint, earthy scent of living stone.

A fictional future, created with AI.

How would a city that constantly renews itself, like a living organism, feel to inhabit?

دبي في عام 2512 قد غطت برج خليفة الأيقوني بمواد هندسية حية تنمو وتصلح نفسها وتتوهج بلطف على طول كل حافة من حواف المدينة. هذا الابتكار يحافظ على أسطح المدينة نقية باستمرار، نابضة بالحياة، وموفرة للطاقة، بينما يخلق جمالية عضوية فريدة. المباني تتلألأ بضوء حيوي ناعم ليلاً، الممرات مبطنة بأسطح ذاتية الإصلاح، ويحمل الهواء رائحة ترابية خفيفة من الحجر الحي.

مستقبل خيالي، صنعه الذكاء الاصطناعي.

كيف سيكون الشعور بالعيش في مدينة تجدد نفسها باستمرار، ككائن حي؟
